name: SNIPE Hunt
full_name: Search for Non-Interacting Particles Experimental Hunt
summary: Synchronized magnetic measurements at multiple field stations, using Earth and its ionosphere as a conversion system for ultralight dark matter.
detection_principle: Axions interacting with the geomagnetic field, or dark photons interacting with conducting boundaries, produce oscillating magnetic fields with characteristic spatial patterns; correlations between sites reject local noise.

sites.name: Multiple low-magnetic-noise field stations in the United States
sites.location: Multiple low-magnetic-noise field stations in the United States

status.label: Published experimental record; current overall operating status unverified
status.evidence: 2023 sources support the phase recorded here, rather than a real-time status of the entire project as of the access date.

timeline.event: A Hunt for Magnetic Signatures of Hidden-Photon and Axion Dark Matter in the Wilderness

collaboration.name: SNIPE Hunt Collaboration / project team
collaboration.participants_note: Only documented principal institutions are listed; full author and affiliation lists are in the sources. Collaborating-institution addresses are not substituted for detector locations.

results.summary: No dark-matter magnetic-field evidence; limits were obtained on kinetic mixing and axion–photon coupling.

science_scope: Directly searches for Galactic-halo axions, axionlike particles or other ultralight dark matter. Limits depend on assumed local density, velocity distribution and coupling models; separate scanned mass intervals do not amount to exclusion of the entire range.
